anya: Heads-up — after the kernel-picker v2 rollout we’re seeing a host-side parse + tokenization P99 bump (~12-18%) for short requests (<=64 tokens). Small requests only, long ones unaffected.

kyle: Reproable across regions?

anya: Yes, eu-west + us-west. Tail spikes correlate with increased syscall counts and a shift in batch shapes.

brian: Any pprof / flamegraph?

anya: Paste from pprof (top of stack):
```
(pprof) top 10
  38.7%  runtime:proto_unmarshal
  22.1%  runtime:tokenize_stream
  12.3%  net:writev -> grpc smallwrite path
   9.4%  kvcache:lookup (miss path)
   6.5%  batching:shape_eval -> kernel_selector
```

jamal: Hmm looks like proto_unmarshal + tokenize_stream dominating. kernel_selector shows up but smaller — could be downstream effect.

anya: Also noticed an increase in mini-batch creation: more batches of size 1-2 instead of 8-16. That pushes different kernel lanes and changes kv cache locality.

kyle: Do we have kvcache hit ratios pre/post?

anya: Quick numbers: pre-rollout host sample: hit=82%, miss=18%. post-rollout same hosts: hit=58%, miss=42%.

brian: That’s a big change. If kernel-picker is changing sequence-length bucketing the cache key distribution might change -> more cold lookups.

jamal: infra-bot, what deployed with kernel-picker v2?

infra-bot: Deploy log: kernel-picker v2 (sha: abc123) rolled to prod 2026-03-21T18:22:11Z across user-facing hosts. No other preparse or tokenizer changes in that window.

kyle: Two orthogonal causes: (1) kernel-picker assigns different batch shapes -> affects batching heuristics + kv cache locality, (2) change caused increase in small writes (writev) and syscalls. We can test both mitigation knobs separately.

anya: Repro steps I used: 6 clients each sending 32-token prompts at 20 qps for 2 mins to a single host; collect pprof + kvcache metrics. Latency delta shows at ~30s after rollout.

brian: Proposed short-term mitigations:
- force batching_heuristic=legacy for <=64 tokens (config)
- raise grpc small-write coalescing threshold (grpc_max_small_write=16384)
- revert kernel-picker on a canary if metrics don’t improve

kyle: I can flip batching_heuristic for a 5% canary. Jamal can run the revert canary and collect pprof.

jamal: Starting canary now (5% traffic to kp-v1) and enabling detailed pprof + kvcache export to logs. Will report in 10m.

anya: Also, note: cheap wins in tokenize path — we can micro-optimize proto_unmarshal and reduce copies. Patch to avoid one memcpy reduced tokenize time by ~6% in local bench.

brian: Good. If kvcache is the root, should also look at key normalization — kernel-picker might be adding metadata to cache keys.

anya: Confirmed: kp-v2 added `seq_bucket` to cache key. That was intended to avoid cross-bucket pollution but it fragments the keyspace.

kyle: Ah — that explains it. seq_bucket in key + more small batches -> much higher cardinality. We should revert key change and instead track bucket in metadata only for kernel selection.

brian: Agreed. Plan: (A) rollback cache-key change in kp-v2 (hotfix), (B) run canary with legacy batching for <=64 tokens, (C) micro-ops in proto_unmarshal.

jamal: Can do (A) later today, (B) started now, (C) can PR microcopy later this sprint.

anya: Filing tracking issue: https://redwood/issue/4567 — notes, pprof snapshot, kvcache diffs, deployment timeline.

kyle: tl;dr: kernel-picker added seq_bucket into kvcache key -> fragmentation -> increased misses -> smaller batches -> different kernel path -> host-side syscall/writev overhead -> P99 tail.

brian: Nice breakdown. Thanks, team. Keep updates in thread. :thumbsup:
